messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failure happens in the test testGetTypeArguments when calling TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Other.class, This.class) and expecting to get 2 type arguments assigned. The issue, according to the bug report, is that TypeUtils.getTypeArguments misses type arguments for partially-assigned classes.

Looking into the TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Type, Class<?>) method (lines 533-535), it delegates to a private overloaded method getTypeArguments(Type, Class<?>, Map), which recursively deals with various Type implementations (Class, ParameterizedType, GenericArrayType, etc).

For the Class<?> version of getTypeArguments (lines 650-681), the code first checks assignability, deals with primitives, copies or creates a map for type assignments, and then checks if the target class has been reached. The check is at line 675:
```
if (cls.getTypeParameters().length > 0 || toClass.equals(cls)) {
    return typeVarAssigns;
}
```
This means if the current class still declares type parameters (i.e., is generic but not yet fully resolved), it returns the assignments immediately without walking up the inheritance hierarchy further.

This looks suspicious. Usually, to resolve type assignments fully, even if the class is generic, you should continue traversing parents/interfaces to fully resolve types to the target class.

The next step (line 680) is walking up the hierarchy by calling getTypeArguments on the closest parent type:
```
return getTypeArguments(getClosestParentType(cls, toClass), toClass, typeVarAssigns);
```

Due to the premature return on a class having type parameters (line 675-677), the code skips this step. That likely causes missing type arguments for partially assigned generic classes, as the recursive resolution is not performed.

The getClosestParentType method (lines 797-835) tries to find the closest generic interface or superclass that inherits from the target class.

Hence, the fault occurs because when the current class is generic (has type parameters), the code in getTypeArguments(Class, Class, Map) returns early without traversing up the hierarchy to resolve the type arguments fully.

The failing test expects for the class Other (likely partially parametrized) to get two assigned type variables for This.class, but due to the early return, the type arguments are incomplete or missing, causing the assertion failures.

Recent bug reports are unrelated, so they are not considered.

Summary:
- The bug is caused by the premature return when cls.getTypeParameters().length > 0 in TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(Class, Class, Map).
- It prevents recursive walking up the inheritance tree to resolve type variable assignments fully.
- Hence, partially assigned generic classes miss their full type argument assignments.

This matches the provided test failure and bug report description.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
